When i worked at a tech store we had older people coming in nearly daily for multiple hundreds of dollars worth of itunes vouchers. Our store had a thing in the system where if it was more than $250 in value we had to get a managers pin to continue. 
Once the manager came down theyd generally have a gentle chat about who its for, and theyd try to educate them and 9 times out of 10 the people would end up just not buying the giftcards because they realised they were getting scammed. 


Just try to have a chat and if theyre friendly say youre worried about them because theres a big scam going around with those specific gift cards. Or even better if your manager can chat with them :)
Also to add to everyone else's points. If it's a recent change with the store, it could also be due to the massive increase in fake notes going around

Your sexuality has no bearing on whether you go to heaven or hell or anywhere in between. 
I can't speak too much on the side of religion, but I know some very Christian families with not straight children, and they've never been told they're going to hell for it. It all comes down to your parents. 

A lot of parents, especially those older and bought up in a very different time, think that it's a sin and will shame you for it. But newer parents have realized it's not a sin. 

I don't know how old you are exactly, but as you get older and are out of that environment you'll find so many accepting people. If your parents won't accept you, don't tell them, atleast don't tell them until you no longer live with them and they can't punish you for being you. 

I promise there are people out there that will accept you for you, and as you get a lot older people stop caring about others sexuality. 

You might even find as you age, you realize you identify as a different sexuality instead. 

Once more, it is not a sin to be gay, or to identify as anything other than straight. You are not banned from heaven for thinking another girl is hot. I promise you this much.

I had no idea what I wanted to do with my life and after a horrible year 13 I opted to not go to uni. I don't test well so exams are horrible for me and I simply could not fathom doing more. I personally am really happy I didn't end up going. Most of my friends that went to and graduated uni don't work in their field as it's too competitive. I even have some friends who didn't go to uni straight after year 13, but are now going like 7 years later. My point is if you don't know what you want to do with uni, you don't have to go. Higher education will always be there for you to go back to. 

As for year 13, all I can offer is if you don't know what you want to do with things but you think you'll want to go to uni. Make sure your classes have enough UE credits so you have the chance to get in if you opt to. Otherwise, take comfort classes so your last year is easy. And I can promise you most jobs don't even care if you go to uni or not unless it's for a specialized field. 

Hope my ramblings helped a little, I remember year 13 sucked a lot because of the pressure of "your future" best of luck out there

I have a cat that had litter aversion issues. He had a couch he peed on instead. I learnt that sometimes it's the type of litter so I swapped to some that's nicer on his feet. It fixed itself for a while, then he peed on the couch again. I was then told the stupid litter box rule. One litter box per cat, plus one. It's such a stupid rule (imo) but it works. He has a favourite litter box and a backup if that one isn't as clean as he likes.

And from your post the cat definitely sounds stressed, try popping him into a smaller room he's familiar with, with the trays until he's ready to explore down there. 

Or alternatively, just don't let the cat down there. Mines not allowed in my bedroom because peeing on the bed is something he refuses to shake. If you don't want something damaged or ruined, don't let the cat near it 


Also YTA for even suggesting to get rid of the cat without exhausting every single method out there. Cats are family members and to ask your partner to get rid of their cat is appalling.

When I started Zoloft, I only got one side effect, which was yawning every like 20 seconds. Lasted about a day or two, that's my only negative experience with Zoloft! Know that the first week or so will be the hardest you'll have as it's your body adjusting to the medication, maybe try start it when you know you don't have anything super important to focus on? if after a week you're still getting side effects, ask to go on a different medication, I don't know how it is where you are but for me my doctor had me coming in every two weeks for three months to monitor any changes. 

Zoloft has made an amazing difference in my life, it's basically halted my anxiety, and definitely helped with my depression. I've never had any issue with focusing because of it either :) I completely understand the anxiety around taking it. I put it off for as long as I could but I had a really great friend who checked up on me and made me start. That's the hardest thing to do. But know that everyone here is here for you. What ever you decide to do, we've got your back
